records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — A calendar update failure is returned after the attendee rows have already been committed, leaving the booking and external calendar out of sync.
records.rationale: The diff shows attendees are committed via prisma.booking.update (createMany) before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` in addGuests.handler.ts, and only sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try/catch — the calendar update is not. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation errors out with DB rows already persisted, leaving booking and external calendar out of sync. The mechanism described is verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — A calendar update failure is returned after the new attendees have already been committed, leaving retries unable to restore calendar state or send invitations.
records.rationale: The diff shows `prisma.booking.update` with `attendees: { createMany: ... }` committing new guests to the DB, then `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with no rollback or error handling around it (unlike the subsequent sendAddGuestsEmails which has try/catch). If updateCalendarAttendees fails, the handler throws while guests remain persisted and calendar invitations were never sent; a retry would hit the existing-attendee filter path. Real atomicity/correctness defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed and the mutation reports success even though the promised guest notifications were not sent.
records.rationale: The diff shows `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` followed by an unconditional `return { message: "Guests added" }`. A failure to send the promised guest-notification emails is swallowed (only console-logged) and the mutation reports success, so the client shows 'Guests added' success toast even when notifications failed. This is verifiable directly in the added addGuests.handler.ts and constitutes broken/incorrect behavior (silent failure masked as success), not a style nit.

records.rationale: The diff explicitly wraps sendAddGuestsEmails in try/catch with only console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') and then unconditionally returns { message: 'Guests added' }, so a failure to send invitation emails is hidden from the caller while guests were persisted — a verifiable silent-failure defect introduced by this code.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Email-send failures are swallowed after partial Promise.all delivery with no retry or durable recovery, while the mutation reports success.
records.rationale: The diff verifiably shows `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log(...) }` in addGuests.handler.ts, after which the handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. Since sendAddGuestsEmails uses `Promise.all`, one rejected email can abort remaining sends after partial delivery, and the client sees success with no error surfaced, retry, or compensation — a real silent-failure path introduced by this diff. Borderline intentional best-effort pattern, so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — Team admins who are not owners are rejected because the admin and owner checks are combined with AND.
records.rationale: The diff shows `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, ...)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, ...))` — the AND means a user must be both admin and owner; a team admin who is not an owner fails the check (as does an owner who is not an admin), so the variable name and evident intent (either role suffices) are contradicted. This is a real correctness defect in the new authorization logic.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The public mutation accepts duplicate guest emails, so direct callers can create duplicate attendee records and send duplicate invitations despite the UI-only uniqueness check.
